raw.assessment: The incumbent produces embedded-caption previews and retains earlier previews, supporting installation review and access to delivered versions. H1-O7 limits any account that full rendering is inherently too slow: nine single-correction sessions completed in five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. H1-O3 and H1-O4 support investigating ordering and source identification, but do not establish their causal contribution to the ten late sessions. The sampled 49 processing hours do not establish festival capacity. Success remains unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: identify each request before rendering with a stable identifier bound to immutable video and caption snapshots; display that identifier and caption wording on completion and download, and verify worker input hashes against the request.
openings.delta: Replace inference from editor filenames and completion numbers with explicit source pairing, while retaining delivered snapshots and embedded-caption rendering on existing private accounts.
openings.prediction: Reversed completion order will no longer change which source pair an editor identifies or downloads; mismatched worker inputs will be rejected before delivery.
openings.probe: In private staging, use fabricated footage to submit two cuts and several caption revisions, reverse completion order, and inject one input mismatch. Have both editors identify the intended preview and reopen the delivered version's original captions. Check source hashes and identification time.
assumptions: Snapshot binding and interface changes fit four engineer-days; this requires estimation.
Staging and review share the one editor-day and remain within the 80-hour allowance.

openings.claim: Do late sessions lose most time before the intended render becomes available, or after availability while identifying and reviewing it?
openings.delta: Distinguishes rendering delay from preview-use delay rather than treating total elapsed time as rendering cost.
openings.prediction: A rendering-delay account predicts late availability; an identification/review account predicts prompt availability followed by a long interval to correctly identified preview.
openings.probe: During the same staging exercise, record final edit, request, worker start, completion, correct selection, and review completion timestamps; compare single-correction and repeated-edit trials.
assumptions: Staging timings discriminate mechanisms but cannot establish the 30-session success target or festival capacity.

raw.assessment: Version mistakes and reversed completion order are observed; their contribution to delay is unmeasured. Both combinations are hypotheses. Keep all assets on existing private accounts, preserve the previous delivery and original captions, and retain embedded-caption delivery. Cap implementation and probes at four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours per week; feasibility and festival demand remain unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: combine immutable input manifests with pending-request coalescing at the render-queue admission interface. Each manifest binds video hash, caption hash and editor intent; coalescing replaces only unstarted requests for that editing branch. Completion publishes against its manifest, and an older completion cannot replace the intended-preview pointer.
openings.delta: Manifest binding alone leaves redundant rendering; coalescing alone can accelerate an unintended pairing. Together they could reduce queue pressure while making the surviving request and its result identifiable. Preserve delivered manifests and their assets independently of pending work.
openings.prediction: Under overlapping saves, the combination produces fewer rendered jobs than manifests alone and fewer pairing mistakes than coalescing alone; benefit may be small for isolated corrections.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging footage in a bounded four-condition comparison: neither mechanism, each alone, both. Force reversed completions and a video-cut change. Record job count, processing time, identification time and hash correctness; verify prior delivery access. Then assess the 30-session target if the remaining resource budget permits.
assumptions: Pending jobs can be replaced without deleting retained assets.
Queue waiting or identification accounts for meaningful delay.
Changes fit the stipulated implementation budget.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: combine a timed browser caption overlay with a shared immutable input bundle at the preview-to-delivery handoff. Editors inspect wording and timing over the identified video immediately; an explicit embedded render consumes that same bundle and returns its identity.
openings.delta: An overlay alone can drift from the delivered render; a shared bundle alone still requires rendering every wording check. Together they could shorten iteration while maintaining a traceable correspondence to final delivery.
openings.prediction: Editors make fewer full renders while identifying the intended pair faster, provided overlay timing agrees sufficiently with embedded playback.
openings.probe: Within the shared budget, compare overlay-only, bundle-only and combined prototypes on fabricated clips with cut changes, overlapping captions and boundary timestamps. Have editors inspect wording and timing, then compare the embedded result. Measure render count, identification time and timing disagreements; disagreements prevent treating the overlay as validated delivery evidence.
assumptions: Existing private infrastructure supports usable browser playback.
Overlay and embedded-render timing can be aligned within budget.
Enough checks can use the overlay to offset its implementation cost.

openings.claim: Bind requests to immutable source snapshots; expose identity and wording; reject worker hash mismatches.
openings.probe: Stage two cuts and revisions, reverse completions, inject mismatch; check identification time and original delivered captions.

openings.claim: Distinguish render availability delay from selection/review delay.
openings.discriminator: Late availability versus long delay after availability.
openings.probe: Timestamp final edit, request, worker start, completion, correct selection and review; compare isolated and repeated edits.
openings.uncertainty: Staging cannot establish session target or festival capacity.

openings.claim: Combine manifests binding hashes and editor intent with branch-specific coalescing of unstarted requests; prevent older completions replacing intended-preview pointer.
openings.discriminator: Combination reduces jobs versus manifests alone and pairing errors versus coalescing alone.
openings.probe: Four conditions: neither, each alone, both; force cut changes/reversed completions; measure jobs, processing, identification, hashes and delivery access.
openings.uncertainty: Queue benefit, safe replacement and budget fit unproven; isolated corrections may gain little.

openings.claim: Combine timed browser overlay with immutable bundle reused by explicit embedded rendering.
openings.discriminator: Fewer renders and faster identification with adequate playback agreement.
openings.fit: Uncertain; private browser playback and timing alignment required.
openings.probe: Compare overlay-only, bundle-only and combined; test cut changes, overlaps and boundary timestamps against embedded output.
openings.uncertainty: Disagreements prevent delivery-evidence claims; usage and implementation payoff unknown.

post_distill.decision: Start with shared D1/D2 staging. Bound all work to four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours weekly; use existing private accounts, retain embedded delivery and previous delivery/original wording. Prioritize alternatives using measured delay. Synthetic evidence leaves 30-session success and festival capacity unproven.
